sentences.text: On December 20, 2018, a putative securities class action lawsuit was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York against Group Inc. and certain former officers of the firm alleging violations of the anti-fraud provisions of the Exchange Act with respect to Group Inc.'s disclosures and public statements concerning 1MDB and seeking unspecified damages.

On June 28, 2021, the court dismissed the claims against one of the individual defendants but denied the defendants' motion to dismiss with respect to the firm and the remaining individual defendants.

Antitrust and Other Litigation: In 2018, a putative class action was filed against Citigroup, CGMI, Citigroup Financial Products Inc., Citigroup Global Markets Holdings Inc., Banamex, Grupo Banamex, and other banks, captioned IN RE MEXICAN GOVERNMENT BONDS ANTITRUST LITIGATION, in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York.
In November 2020, the court granted defendants' motion to dismiss, and the plaintiffs appealed.

comparisons.peer_summary: The monetary relief class action settled for ~$6.2 billion with $700 million returned to defendants; a separate injunctive class action saw preliminary approval denied in June 2024, while individual actions by opting merchants have mostly settled representing over 70% of sales volume. Ongoing matters include a Swiss EURIBOR investigation and a U.S. Court of Appeals affirmation of a dismissal in an antitrust lawsuit; the Firm has resolved all non-U.S. dollar LIBOR actions and obtained dismissals or moved for summary judgment in remaining U.S. dollar LIBOR cases.

Both disclosures highlight the firm's exposure to large-scale class actions where certification status significantly impacts the litigation trajectory.
